cover.headline: The ships come back. So does the risk.
cover.deck: Gemini sends its last three North Europe loops back through Suez, just as the Houthis take Yemen's Red Sea coast and threaten Saudi ports. Asia–Med was the only main container lane to rise last week. Sixteen pages on what that means for cargo that touches Egypt.
cover.standfirst: Drewry counted 57 container ships through the Suez Canal in the week to 15 November, up 73% on a year earlier, and Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd will move three more Asia–Europe services to the canal from 4 December. In the same week Far East–Mediterranean spot rates rose 6.8% to $4,989 a box while every other main lane fell, and Red Sea transits at Bab el-Mandeb dropped 28% from their October peak.

pages.title: The briefing
pages.label: If you read one page, read this

columns.text: Welcome to Voyage 002 of *The Rockit Manifest*, our Monday review for exporters, importers, manufacturers and fellow forwarders who move cargo through Egypt. Last week we promised four follow-ups: December rates, APEC in Shenzhen, the IMO carbon vote and the rebate briefing. All four are inside, including where we could not verify what was said.

Every figure is footnoted to the page we read it on. Where a claim comes from one side of a conflict, we say so. *Why it matters* and *Rockit's read* are our analysis, kept apart from the reporting. — **The Rockit desk, Cairo**

items: **Ocean:** Asia–Med was the only main lane to rise: Xeneta +6.8% to $4,989 per 40ft, Drewry Shanghai–Genoa +6% to $4,436. Maersk's $1,500 Med peak surcharge applies from today.
**December:** MSC, Hapag-Lloyd and CMA CGM have filed $6,500–6,800 per 40ft for Asia to the East Med.
**Red Sea:** Gemini moves three more loops to Suez from 4 Dec, but the Houthis now hold Yemen's Red Sea coast and told ships to leave Saudi ports.
**Hormuz:** transits fell again to 115 out / 148 in; attacks worldwide were the highest since mid-October.
**Air:** global rates $3.45/kg, +31% y/y; Middle East–Europe +66%; Saudi air tonnage down a third.
**Policy:** no verified trade deal came out of Shenzhen, so the 9–10 January deadlines stand.
**Egypt:** IMF staff-level deal puts about $2.3bn on the table before 15 December; September imports +29.7%.
**Money:** CBE deposit rate 20.0%; the dollar back above EGP 54 on 22 Nov; Goldman sees a hold until late Q1.
**Importing from Asia?** Spot to the Med is rising towards December's tariffs. Book early in December, and get the peak, fuel, piracy and Suez surcharges named in writing.
**Shipping to or via Saudi Red Sea ports?** Ask your carrier what happens to your box if Jeddah calls are suspended, and confirm war-risk cover on the Red Sea leg.
**Signing 2027 contracts?** Wait for Hapag-Lloyd's Suez-based fuel rates on 1 December and the IMO decision on 4 December before you fix fuel and carbon terms.

columns.head: Every lane fell except ours
columns.deck: Asia–Med spot rose 6–7% last week while every other main lane slipped. Egypt's importers now pay about $1,550 a box more than North Europe's.
text: Drewry's World Container Index fell 3% to $4,176 per 40ft on 19 November, its fourth weekly fall, because transpacific rates dropped. Shanghai–Genoa, Drewry's closest proxy for Egypt's Mediterranean ports, went the other way: up 6% to $4,436 after three flat weeks. Shanghai–Rotterdam held at $3,496.

Xeneta's data show the same split. Far East–Mediterranean spot rose 6.8% to $4,989 per 40ft, while Far East–North Europe fell 2.3% to $3,438 and every other fronthaul eased. Average Med rates are now $1,551 a box above North Europe. Xeneta ties the move to the Red Sea: Bab el-Mandeb container transits have fallen from 16.6 a day on 25 October to 11.9 on 19 November, and Med trades are the most exposed.
Freightos, whose data run to mid-week, still had Asia–Med flat at about $4,300. The rise came late in the week: check the date of any index you are quoted.
columns.why: Last week the gap between December tariffs and the spot market was about $2,000 a box. This week the three big carriers' December tariffs ($6,500–6,800) sit about $1,500–1,800 above Xeneta's average, and the market is rising towards them. December's increases are more likely to stick on Asia–Med than they were in November; book early in the month and get the surcharges in writing.

columns.head: More ships through Suez, just as the risk rises
columns.deck: Gemini moves its last three North Europe loops back to the canal. In Yemen, the Houthis have taken the Red Sea coast.
text: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd will move their NE1, NE2 and NE3 Asia–North Europe services from the Cape to Suez “on a structural basis”. The first westbound sailings are *Mary Maersk* from Ningbo around 4 December, *Alette Maersk* from Shanghai around 20 December and the 23,700 TEU *Damietta Express* from Shanghai around 14 January. Drewry says 60% of Asia–Europe capacity is back on the Suez route.

The security picture moved the other way. Drewry reports a “material deterioration” around Bab el-Mandeb and warns against extrapolating better traffic into December and January. Reuters reports that the Houthis have seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and pushed government forces back to Aden. The Saudi-led coalition said it struck Hodeidah port on 20 November; Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree told shipping companies to “immediately evacuate their ships” from Saudi Red Sea ports, and the group said it would target ports “in Jeddah and the Red Sea”. Yemen's information minister said Hodeidah remains fully operational. No attack on a merchant ship there was verified in the week.
columns.why: The Suez return is what is pushing capacity and rates down in 2027 forecasts. Keep Cape-routing and war-risk clauses in every Red Sea contract, and for Saudi deliveries ask what the plan is if Jeddah calls are suspended.

columns.title: Port Said and Damietta join Gemini loops

items: **AE11:** Port Said replaces the westbound Tangier call, from *Estelle Maersk* leaving Shanghai on 17 November.
**AE19:** Damietta added, from *Ane Maersk* leaving Xingang on 18 November.
**AE12:** already calls Port Said East both ways; Colombo added from about 12 January.
Maersk lists AE5, AE11, AE12, AE15, AE19, ME1 and ME2 as routed via Suez; NE1–NE3 follow from December.

blocks.text: Hormuz: attacks at their highest since October

UKMTO's weekly overview of 20 November counted 115 outbound and 148 inbound Hormuz transits, down from 139 and 169 a week earlier, and six verified attacks in the period to 18 November. In the Gulf, Orbital Risk counted seven strikes on six ships, four of them tankers within 13nm of Khasab. JMIC rates the threat as SEVERE.

blocks.text: The LPG tanker *TARA GAS* was hit on 16 and 17 November and abandoned; one Indian seafarer is missing. *NAVIG8 MESSI*, managed by ADNOC L&S, was hit on 17 November, with one crew member missing and 11 injured. UKMTO reported further tanker strikes near Khasab on 20 and 21 November. Iran's navy claimed a mine strike east of Hormuz; Reuters could not verify it.

blocks.html: Why it mattersMSC is adding a second Fujairah shuttle (Colombo–Khor Fakkan–Fujairah–Sohar) from December, outside the Strait. For Egypt–Gulf cargo, plan on Gulf of Oman discharge plus trucking, or Saudi gateways, and price in landside congestion (page 7).

columns.head: Bunkers fall; MSC's fuel surcharge rises
text: Ship & Bunker's Global 20 Ports average put VLSFO at $838 a tonne on 20 November, down $25.50 in a week (Fujairah $800, Singapore $842, Rotterdam $705.50); MGO fell to $1,364. Brent was about $92 and has lost roughly 15% in November. MSC's December fuel surcharge nevertheless rises to $304 per TEU from $266.
columns.why: Fuel is cheaper than a month ago. Challenge any December BAF or GFS increase in your quotes.

columns.head: Hapag-Lloyd rewrites its fuel charge
text: From 1 January 2027 Hapag-Lloyd replaces its Marine Fuel Recovery with a Marine Fuel Surcharge based on a full return to Suez routings, reviewed quarterly. First-quarter rates are published on 1 December.
columns.why: A Suez-based fuel charge should come in below the Cape-era one. Compare the 1 December figures before signing 2027 terms.

columns.head: Two in three ships arrive late
text: Drewry says East–West on-time performance fell from 40% in September to 34% in October. It expects 42 blank sailings out of 724 on the main East–West trades in weeks 48–52 (6%); the transpacific accounts for 48% of them, Asia–Europe/Med 33%.
columns.why: Build buffer stock and free-time allowances into December–January plans; Asia–Med capacity cuts are modest, so the rate push rests on surcharges.

columns.head: ZIM's profit jumps to $830m
text: ZIM reported Q3 net income of $830m (Q3 2025: $123m) on revenue of $2.71bn, up 53%. Its average freight rate rose 55% to $2,480 per TEU, and it lifted 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.3–3.5bn.

columns.head: No global carbon price yet; two weeks to decide
text: IMO's GHG working group meets 23–27 November and MEPC 85 runs 30 November–3 December. The resumed session to adopt the Net-Zero Framework is pencilled for 4 December, “subject to confirmation by MEPC 85”. Nine shipping associations, including BIMCO, ICS and WSC, called for a global deal on 18 November without endorsing the current text. The US Federal Maritime Commission chair said on 11 November that the framework “cannot be adopted, will never be enforced”.
columns.why: No global carbon charge reaches freight bills in 2027 either way. EU ETS charges already do: MSC's carbon surcharge to the Med is $133 per TEU.

columns.head: Watchmen strike averted
text: The Pacific Maritime Association and ILWU Local 26 reached a tentative deal on 21 November, averting a strike at Los Angeles and Long Beach. Ratification is pending.

blocks.title: Why Asia–Med moved when everything else fell

blocks.text: Asia–Mediterranean services have no short way around Bab el-Mandeb: for a Med port, the Cape detour adds proportionally far more sailing than it does for Rotterdam. So when Red Sea transits fall, as they did by 28% between 25 October and 19 November, Med capacity tightens first and Med spot rates react first; Xeneta calls these trades the most operationally exposed to the region. That is how one security shock can lift Egypt's freight while the global index falls.

columns.head: Middle East lanes lead a 31% rise
columns.deck: Global air rates are a third above last year. Rates out of the Middle East and South Asia have risen fastest, and Saudi Arabia has lost a third of its air cargo.
text: WorldACD's figures for week 45 (2–8 November) put the global average at $3.45 per kg, up 2% in the week and 31% on a year earlier, while tonnage fell 2%. Middle East & South Asia (MESA) rose most, 63%; MESA–Europe was up 66% and Dubai origins 83%. Africa-origin rates, which include Egypt, rose 7% in a single week. Saudi Arabia's tonnage was 33% below its level before Houthi attacks began in early October.

Freightos data reported by The Loadstar show Europe–US rates up 12% in a week to $3.27 per kg, the highest since December 2022, and China–North America up 16% to $9.25. Asia–Europe space is still available, CH Robinson says.

Gulf hubs are still short of space. Consultancy Aevean says combined capacity at Doha, Dubai and Abu Dhabi is about 12% below pre-conflict levels, roughly 2,200 tonnes a day; Emirates, Qatar Airways and Etihad are back above 2025 levels, but foreign freighter capacity at the three hubs is down 49%. Xeneta sees air rates 5–10% lower in 2027, but only with a lasting Gulf peace deal.
columns.why: Egyptian exporters routing via Gulf hubs should book home-carrier space, not foreign freighters, and budget 2027 air contracts for a no-relief case. Importers from Europe for December delivery should book now.

blocks.head: Cathay grows; AI fills the transpacific
text: Cathay Cargo carried 162,747 tonnes in October, up 7.5%, on capacity up just 0.5%. Korean Air reports “compounded capacity pressure” on the transpacific from Q4 consumer goods plus AI hardware.

blocks.head: DHL buys its own India freighter
text: DHL Global Forwarding launched a twice-weekly 747 freighter linking Hong Kong, Navi Mumbai and Liège, targeting 25–30 tonnes per flight on the India sectors. It expects only about 20 freighters to be delivered worldwide in 2027, mostly to express firms.
blocks.why: With few new freighters coming, shippers without contracted space will compete for what is left.

blocks.head: Bangkok backlog; US recovers
text: Bangkok's Thai Airways cargo terminal still has more than 1,000 lots outstanding after September floods; exports may roll two to three days. US networks recovered by 15–16 November from a four-hour nationwide ground stop on 13 November.

blocks.head: IATA: keep the EU ETS off international flights
text: After ICAO's air transport conference (16–20 November), IATA urged EU states to back CORSIA rather than extend the EU ETS to international flights, and said 2026 passenger growth will be the weakest since 2009 outside the pandemic years.
blocks.why: Weaker passenger growth means less belly space on Cairo routes than airlines planned.

columns.title: What changed for forwarders this week

blocks.text: Two things land directly on our desks. First, airlines' revised Direct Air Waybill terms can make a forwarder liable for a shipper's misdeclaration, so we confirm each carrier's terms before tendering. Second, the EU now charges €5 per line on low-value parcels, which pushes e-commerce sellers towards consolidated shipments into EU warehouses.

columns.head: Forwarders push IATA to rewrite the DAWB
text: The US Airforwarders Association and NCBFAA published a white paper on 16 November asking IATA to amend its revised Direct Air Waybill framework, in force since 1 July. Without a separate airline agreement, they say, a forwarder acting for a named shipper may carry liability for misdeclarations, undeclared dangerous goods and packaging failures. Australia's IFCBAA and Canada's CIFFA back the paper.
columns.why: Shippers: accurate descriptions and DG declarations protect you and your forwarder.

columns.head: Europe's parcel charges bite: −63%
text: The European Commission confirms its €2 handling fee applies from 1 November, on top of the €3 duty per item on parcels up to €150 since 1 July. Its preliminary count shows 555m low-value items entered the EU in Q3, against 1.51bn a year earlier. Each line on a declaration now adds €5.

columns.head: Photos into customs descriptions
text: DHL Express now turns a customer's photo of an item into a customs-compliant description in seconds, live in 10 Americas markets with more in 2027. CargoAi launched CargoQUALITY to benchmark airline and handler stations.
columns.why: Vague descriptions are a leading cause of customs holds, including under Egypt's ACI.

columns.head: UAE landside strain
text: India–Gulf shippers face booking curbs, congestion at Khor Fakkan and empty-return charges of up to $1,200 per 40ft to the Sajaa dry port. Emirates SkyCargo and Virgin Atlantic Cargo signed an MoU to widen interline and block-space deals.
columns.why: For Egypt–UAE cargo, allow extra clearance time and ask about empty-return charges.

blocks.text: Turkey is a major sourcing market for Egypt: DFDS, which runs the Trieste–Damietta ro-ro, already owns Ekol's international road business.

columns.head: A summit, a declaration, no trade deal we could verify
columns.deck: We promised to report what came out of APEC in Shenzhen. On trade, nothing we could read on a primary or reliable page.
text: EnterpriseAM reports that Presidents Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen in the first trilateral summit of its kind. The 90-minute talks ended with a joint declaration that “nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought” and a pledge to raise output of refined petroleum products. Wire coverage of the summit was not reachable from our desk, so this is our only account of it.

We found no change to tariffs, to the US port fees on Chinese ships, or to China's rare-earth waivers. A search of the Federal Register for 13–22 November returned no new Section 301 maritime notice. The last primary US statement is USTR's readout of a 6 November call in which Ambassador Greer and Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed Vice Premier He Lifeng to “fully implement” commitments on farm purchases, rare earths and critical minerals.

Washington did act on technology. A Commerce Department rule effective 19 November requires licences for advanced chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, restricts remote computing for China-linked firms, and warns of “import restrictions” for countries that tolerate evasion. USTR's Greer wrote on 16 November that 19 trading partners, nearly 40% of world GDP, have signed deals with the US.
columns.why: Until an official notice says otherwise, US-lane and Asia-lane quotes that run past 9 January need a reopener clause. Shipments of servers or GPUs routed via Southeast Asian hubs face end-user checks.

blocks.text: US Central Command said on 18 November that ships taking Iranian cargo by ship-to-ship transfer “may be stopped, boarded, diverted, captured”, even outside Iranian waters. US warplanes struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island on 17 November, a US official told Bloomberg; Iran's Mehr agency reported no casualties. Treasury officials pressed Singapore and Malaysia on sanctions compliance. Qatar is still mediating, and Bloomberg reports neither side willing to compromise.

columns.title: Restrictions at a record
columns.note: Import restrictions in force now cover $5.4tn, 21.3% of world imports: the highest since monitoring began in 2009.

items.label: ships attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July
people and entities added to EU Russia sanctions (12 + 101)
cap on international credits in CBAM carbon-price deductions
world imports under restrictions (21.3%)

blocks.head: A wheat ship bound for Egypt sinks
text: The *BETUL 8*, carrying almost 3,000 tonnes of wheat from Tulcea in Romania to Egypt, capsized off Bulgaria on 16 November; crew told Bulgarian media it was hit by two sea drones. All 12 were rescued and no one has been officially blamed. The LPG tanker *GAS HUSKY* sank off Bulgaria the next day.
blocks.why: The Romanian and Bulgarian coastal route, Egypt's safer alternative to Odesa, is now in the line of fire. Expect higher war-risk premiums on Danube and Constanța loadings.

blocks.head: EU targets the shadow fleet's managers
text: On 16 November the EU listed 12 people and 101 entities, including ship managers and traders in the UAE, Oman, Seychelles and China, a Dubai network, and Moscow's Balance Insurance; gCaptain reports nearly 50 Russian banks were added as well.
blocks.why: Several listed managers sit in Dubai, a common counterparty hub. Run KYC on UAE ship managers and insurers for any EU-linked cargo.

blocks.head: CBAM credit for carbon paid abroad, but not for Egypt
text: Commission Regulation 2026/2498 (16 November) lets importers deduct carbon prices effectively paid outside the EU, with international credits capped at 10%. CBAM extends to Norway and Iceland from 1 January 2027, and the EU and UK agreed on 20 November to link their emissions trading systems, paving the way for mutual CBAM exemption.
blocks.why: Egypt has no national carbon price, so its steel, aluminium, fertiliser and cement exporters get no deduction, while UK rivals move towards exemption.

blocks.head: Egypt left off the EU's draft scrap list
text: EnterpriseAM reports that the Commission's September draft list of non-OECD countries allowed to receive EU metal scrap leaves Egypt out; exports to unlisted countries would be banned from 21 May 2027. Cairo is lobbying to be added.
blocks.why: The EU supplies about half of Egypt's ferrous scrap, per EnterpriseAM's sources. A ban would reshape bulk imports into Alexandria and Damietta.

blocks.head: The EU's new customs authority meets
text: The EU Customs Authority held its first management board in Lille on 19 November. It will run EU-wide risk analysis and the Customs Data Hub that replaces more than 100 national systems, starting in 2027.
blocks.why: EU-level risk targeting will make HS codes and product data on Egyptian export filings matter more.

columns.head: The IMF deal lands before the deadline
columns.deck: Staff agreed the final reviews on 18 November. About $2.3bn now needs only the Board's signature before 15 December.
text: The IMF and Egypt reached staff-level agreement on the eighth and final review of the Extended Fund Facility and the third review of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility. If the Executive Board approves before the programme expires on 15 December, Egypt receives about $1.5bn under the EFF and up to about $0.8bn under the RSF, bringing total disbursements to about $9.6bn.

Goldman Sachs expects the CBE to hold at 20% until late Q1 2027, and sees the pound at 53, 52 and 50 per dollar over three, six and twelve months. In bank trading the dollar rose back above EGP 54 on 22 November; the last CBE quote we could read was 53.39 on 12 November. Net reserves were $57.5bn at end-October.
CAPMAS data show September imports up 29.7% to $10.6bn and exports up 7.4% to $5.3bn; the deficit widened 60.6% to $5.3bn.
columns.why: The IMF deal removes last week's biggest FX risk, but the Fund wants the pound to move with shocks, not be held flat. Keep FX clauses in freight quotes and expect a 53–55 working range.

columns.title: What we can confirm, and what we can't

blocks.text: The Finance and Investment ministries briefed exporters on the revamped rebate programme on 15 November as scheduled. We could not read any report of what was said there: every outlet that covered it was unreachable from our desk, so we are not repeating figures we only saw in search snippets.

The rules on record are unchanged: rebates up 35% on average from November shipments; the state pays 50% of sea and land freight to Africa, Latin America, Australia, Southeast Asia and Russia; 25% of air freight to Europe and 50% to the UK for agricultural exports; 25% of domestic transport, cargo insurance and express-vessel invoices. Files must be complete before they are accepted. The FY 2026/27 budget sets aside EGP 48bn.

columns.text: What the rules mean for your paperwork

items: Freight invoice, B/L and insurance certificate in the exporter's name, dated and itemised.
Inland trucking invoice kept separately (a 25% line of its own).
Shipments since 1 November qualify; phase one ends 31 December.
Payment timing has not been published on any page we could read.

blocks.head: More ways to move a box between Egyptian ports
text: Yang Ming is taking slots on DP World feeders marketed as EG1–EG3, linking Port Said, Damietta, Alexandria and El Dekheila. Sidra Line's revised loop runs Alexandria–Misurata–Rades–Casablanca–Conakry with a 750 TEU ship. The EBRD lent logistics firm Mesco up to EGP 585m for trucks and yard works at Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta and Sokhna.
blocks.why: Intra-Egypt feeders make it easier to book a mainline call at Port Said or Damietta with on-carriage to Alexandria on one carrier.

blocks.head: A Sokhna–Jebel Ali corridor for Egyptian produce
text: Majid Al Futtaim and DP World signed an MoU to move more Egyptian fruit and vegetables to MAF's UAE stores: consolidation in cold stores at Sokhna, DP World feeders to the UAE, then refrigerated moves to Jebel Ali. No investment value, volume or timeline was given.
blocks.why: The route runs through Hormuz, where risk is rising. It is an MoU only, so timing is open.

blocks.head: Pay more for gas, keep exporting
text: Seven fertiliser makers agreed to pay $175m upfront under a 45-day deal that began on 16 November, Asharq Business reports via EnterpriseAM. Their gas price rises 50% to $12.75/mmBtu; in return they can export all current output until early January, while gas cuts of 20–40% stay.
blocks.why: Urea and ammonia exporters can plan December liftings, but in smaller parcels, with a policy review in January.

blocks.head: Damietta firm becomes the first non-EU verifier
text: Damietta-based ISSC is the first verification body outside the EU accredited under CBAM, EnterpriseAM reports, so Egyptian cement, fertiliser, aluminium and steel exporters can have emissions data verified at home. Egypt supplied 44.3% of the EU's non-EU urea imports in 2025.

blocks.head: India aims for $12bn; China at $20bn
text: Egypt and India set a target of $12bn of trade by 2030, up from $6.5bn, and agreed to explore a free trade agreement and speed up India's industrial zone in SCZone. The investment minister put Egypt–China trade at about $20bn.

blocks.head: Agreements signed; border raised
text: Egypt and Libya's GNU signed agreements and MoUs on gas infrastructure, refining, fisheries, SMEs and labour on 19 November. Libya, Egypt's largest African market at $1.2bn in nine months, raised visas and entry through the border crossing; no trade-facilitation measure was named.

blocks.head: Saudi ports in the Houthis' sights
text: After the 20 November warning to ships in Saudi Red Sea ports, watch services that call both Jeddah and Sokhna. MSC's new North India–Red Sea loop (Mundra, Port Qasim, Jeddah, King Abdullah Port) starts in late November with 2,500–3,000 TEU ships.
blocks.why: For Saudi-bound cargo, ask for a contingency: Gulf-side ports, or Safaga and Sokhna ferries with trucking.

blocks.head: Building around Hormuz
text: An ADNOC L&S tanker was attacked in Hormuz on 17 November. A former WEF supply-chain head told EnterpriseAM that Maersk charges “USD 1k a container to cross Hormuz”; we have not seen the carrier's tariff. Saudi road-freight registrations rose 52% to 104,612 in Q3.

blocks.head: Minimum wage up 21% in January
text: The private-sector minimum wage rises 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering 26.5m workers.
blocks.why: Expect upward pressure on local trucking, warehousing and handling tariffs from January.

blocks.text: Customs watch: we found no new customs decree, ACI/Nafeza change or GOEIC rule dated 16–22 November on any page we could read.

pages.title: The toolkit
pages.label: Practical · Red Sea cargo in December

blocks.title: Six questions before you book Red Sea cargo this December

blocks.text: Ships are returning to Suez while the security picture around Bab el-Mandeb and Saudi Red Sea ports worsens. A booking that looks cheap can carry costs that only show up when routing changes. These six lines cover most of them.

blocks.html:
AskWhyWhat a good answer looks like
RoutingServices can switch between Suez and the CapeThe service name, its routing today, and transit days both ways
Diversion clauseIf the ship reroutes, who pays the extra days and fuel?A named surcharge, or a cap, written into the quote
War-riskPremiums can be added mid-voyageThe current charge per box and how it is reviewed
Skipped callsJeddah or Sokhna may be omitted at short noticeWhere the box would be discharged, and who pays on-carriage
SurchargesDecember adds peak, fuel, piracy and Suez chargesEvery line named, with its effective date
Free timeTwo in three East–West ships arrive lateDemurrage and detention days that start from actual, not scheduled, arrival

items: Benchmark Asia quotes against $4,300–4,989 per 40ft spot (Freightos, Drewry, Xeneta), dated 17–19 November.
Maersk's $1,500 per 40ft Med peak surcharge applies from 23 November; check it is in your quote.
Challenge fuel-surcharge increases: bunker prices fell $25.50 a tonne in a week.
Price FX risk: the dollar went back above EGP 54 on 22 November.
Libya, Sudan, Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia are 50%-freight-support markets: keep freight files complete.
Perishables to the Gulf: plan for Hormuz risk; MAF's Sokhna–Jebel Ali corridor is an MoU only.
CBAM goods to the EU: emissions data can now be verified in Damietta.
Air to Europe or the Gulf: rates from the region are 63–83% above last year; book early.
Get written confirmation of each airline's DAWB terms before tendering.
Keep a 9–10 January reopener in US- and China-lane quotes.
Screen UAE ship managers and insurers against the 16 November EU listings.
Agree a contingency for Saudi Red Sea calls with each carrier.

columns.html:
FAK · Freight All Kinds: a carrier's published base rate for general cargo, regardless of commodity.
PSS · Peak Season Surcharge: an add-on charged in busy periods.
GFS / MFS · Global Fuel Surcharge (MSC) / Marine Fuel Surcharge (Hapag-Lloyd from 2027): the fuel component of a sea rate.
TEU / FEU · Twenty- and forty-foot equivalent units: one 40ft box is two TEU.
WCI / FBX · Drewry World Container Index and Freightos Baltic Index: weekly spot-rate benchmarks.
Blank sailing · A scheduled voyage a carrier cancels to cut capacity.
Gemini · The Maersk–Hapag-Lloyd network partnership.
UKMTO / JMIC · UK Maritime Trade Operations and the Joint Maritime Information Center: naval reporting centres for Gulf and Red Sea shipping.
STS · Ship-to-ship transfer of cargo at sea.
DAWB · Direct Air Waybill: an air waybill issued in the shipper's name rather than the forwarder's.
EFF / RSF · The IMF's Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility.
CBAM · EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: a carbon price on imports of steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser and more.
NZF · The IMO Net-Zero Framework: a proposed global carbon price for shipping.
ACI / ACID · Egypt's Advance Cargo Information system and the 19-digit ACID number every import needs before shipment.
